key_insight: ZFO separates "where to go" from "how far to go": it uses a trusted first-order direction and a cheap zeroth-order search to adapt the step size along that direction.
engineering_relevance: This can improve LLM fine-tuning stability and efficiency by avoiding overly conservative fixed steps and reducing the cost of full line search.
method: Use a first-order optimizer to get the descent direction.
Evaluate the objective at two extra points along that direction.
Fit a local 1D model and choose a curvature-aware step within a bounded interval.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that across evaluated language models and datasets, ZFO often improves optimization and final performance over fixed-step first-order baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the chosen direction and the local model; noisy objective estimates or poor interval settings could weaken the step selection.
paper_title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
